candidates.exact_span: Water quality-based requirements are necessary where effluent limits more stringent than technology-based limits are necessary to maintain or achieve federal or state water quality limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes when water-quality-based effluent limits supersede technology-based limits; different readings of this trigger change which numeric limit is selected for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Under Section 301(b)(1)(C) of the CWA, discharges are subject to effluent limitations based on federal or state WQS.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Frames the legal basis for WQS-derived effluent limits; whether this is treated as establishing enforceable numeric limits versus background rationale affects which limits are compared to reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent limitations and/or conditions established in the draft permit are in compliance with applicable State WQS and applicable State water quality management plans to assure that surface WQS of the receiving waters are protected and maintained, or attained.
candidates.computation_change_reason: References effluent limitations and/or conditions tied to State WQS; interpretation of 'conditions' versus numeric effluent limits affects whether a reported value is compared to a numeric limit or treated as non-numeric/report-only.

candidates.exact_span: The facility discharge point into the San Juan River is in State of New Mexico waters approximately two miles upstream of the Navajo Nation’s boundary.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Locates the discharge in New Mexico waters near a downstream tribal boundary; different geographic readings could change which jurisdiction's water quality standards are treated as governing the point of discharge.

candidates.exact_span: Since 40 CFR §122.4(d) requires NPDES permits also be protective of a downstream state or tribe’s water quality standards, the water quality standards of the Navajo Nation have been considered.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Introduces downstream tribal WQS as a permitting consideration; whether Navajo Nation standards are treated as co-applicable or merely considered could change which numeric limits apply to each parameter.

candidates.exact_span: The NPDES permits contain technology-based effluent limitations reflecting the best controls available. Where these technology-based permit limits do not protect water quality or the designated uses, additional water quality-based effluent limitations and/or conditions are included in the NPDES permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Describes a two-tier limit structure (technology-based versus additional water-quality-based limits/conditions); different interpretations of when WQBEL are added change which enforceable numeric limit is selected.

candidates.exact_span: State narrative and numerical water quality standards are used in conjunction with EPA criteria and other available toxicity information to determine the adequacy of technology-based permit limits and the need for additional water quality-based controls.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies inputs used to decide whether additional WQBEL are needed; treating narrative standards, EPA criteria, or toxicity information as operative versus explanatory could change derived numeric limits.

candidates.exact_span: The general and specific stream standards are provided in New Mexico State Standards for Interstate and Intrastate Surface Water (20.6.4 NMAC, effective September 12, 2018).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies the governing New Mexico regulatory citation and effective date for numerical standards; different readings of which NMAC version applies in FY2025 would change applicable numeric limits.

candidates.exact_span: The facility discharges into the San Juan River in segment number 20.6.4.401 of the San Juan Basin.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Assigns the receiving water to a specific 20.6.4 NMAC segment; segment-specific standards can differ, so interpretation of this segment number changes which numeric WQS-derived limits apply.

candidates.exact_span: The designated uses of the receiving waters are public and industrial water supply, irrigation, livestock watering, wildlife habitat, primary contact, marginal coldwater aquatic life and warmwater aquatic life.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Lists designated uses that drive WQS application and limit derivation under 20.6.4 NMAC; adding, omitting, or reclassifying a designated use would change calculated water-quality-based limits.

candidates.exact_span: The general and specific stream standards for the Navajo Nation (NN) are provided in Surface Water Quality Standards (NNWQS) passed by Navajo Nation Resources Committee on May 13, 2008, effective March 26, 2009.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies the governing Navajo Nation standards source and effective date; whether NNWQS are treated as operative for any parameters changes the numeric limit set used in compliance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: The Navajo Nation WQS and New Mexico WQS are very similar and protection to NMWQS at the point of discharge would also be protective of downstream Navajo Nation waters, except for some of the parameters as discussed below.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States that NM and NN standards diverge for some parameters not present in this segment; which parameters are excepted changes the applicable numeric limit (A) and leaves unresolved which standard governs missing or unreported results for those parameters (C).

candidates.exact_span: The Navajo Nation designated uses of the San Juan River at the point it enters the Navajo Nation are domestic water supply, primary human contact, secondary human contact, agricultural water supply, fish consumption, aquatic & wildlife habitat and livestock watering.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Lists downstream Navajo Nation designated uses that may differ from New Mexico uses at the discharge point; different use sets can yield different NN WQS-derived limits if NN standards are treated as applicable.
